by Daryl Ducharme, Open Source Programs Office

This Week in Open Source for October 15, 2026

A look around the world of open source

After speaking about the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol and Model Context Protocol (MCP) in Toronto last week (which I recapped in Tag-Team Transmission), open agent boundaries were clearly still on my mind while collecting this week's reads. As AI agents, terminal tools, and embedded micro-apps move deeper into everyday software workflows, a central tension keeps surfacing across the open source community: where do human judgment, interface trust, and maintainer sustainability fit in? Whether teams are wiring up open protocols in the Unix shell, running multimodal retrieval locally on a laptop, or stewarding decades-old kernel infrastructure, the healthiest open source architectures don't replace human agency—they give workers clearer boundaries, inspectable tools, and a genuine seat at the controls.

Upcoming Events

🗓️ October 2026

  • All Things Open 2026 (October 19–20, 2026) — Raleigh, North Carolina, USA. One of the largest community-focused open source conferences on the U.S. East Coast exploring open source software, AI engineering, and maintainer sustainability—featuring Googlers Andrew Brogdon, Mark Techson, and Marc Dougherty speaking on "Where Is My Futuristic App? Generative UI and the Open Future" and Abdel Sghiouar on "Taming Agentic AI: How to Run Agents-Generated Code Safely on Kubernetes", alongside the Google Community Lounge with the Flutter team.
  • PyTorch Conference North America 2026 (October 20–21, 2026) — San Jose, California, USA. Two days of open source machine learning innovation across the PyTorch ecosystem—featuring a keynote by Google's Bill Jia ("Workload Fungibility in the Age of Agents") and technical sessions from Googlers Chris Jones, Sandeep Pokkunuri, Rob Mulla, Ankita Luthra, Trinadh Kotturu, Claudio Basile, Qi Zhou, Jago Macleod, and Aleksey Vlasenko on TorchTPU, vLLM, SGLang, Ray, and Kubernetes.
  • AGNTCon + MCPCon North America 2026 (October 22–23, 2026) — San Jose, California, USA. Linux Foundation and Agentic AI Foundation conference focused on building and scaling production agentic systems with open standards—featuring keynotes by Google's Sarah Drasner and Chi Wang, plus sessions from Googlers Alan Blount (on A2UI), Junjie Bu (on interoperable agent discovery), Amit Handa (on agentic commerce), Dominic Farolino (on MCP Apps + WebMCP), and Prerna Kakkar & Kurtis Van Gent (on EvalBench).
  • GitHub Universe 2026 (October 28–29, 2026) — San Francisco, California, USA & Virtual. Annual global developer gathering highlighting open source workflows, collaborative security, and multi-model AI-assisted software engineering.

🗓️ November 2026

  • Open Source in Finance Forum (OSFF) New York (November 4–5, 2026) — New York, New York, USA. Dedicated industry conference examining open source compliance, supply-chain security, and collaborative innovation across regulated financial institutions.
  • SeaGL (Seattle GNU/Linux Conference) 2026 (November 6–7, 2026) — Seattle, Washington, USA & Virtual. Free, grassroots technical summit dedicated to spreading awareness and knowledge of free and open source software, hardware, and culture.
  • KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026 (November 9–12, 2026) — Salt Lake City, Utah, USA. The Cloud Native Computing Foundation's flagship conference uniting adopters and maintainers around Kubernetes and cloud-native infrastructure—featuring over 35 sessions and keynotes from Googlers including Abdel Sghiouar, Jago Macleod, Tim Hockin, Kaslin Fields, John Belamaric, Dawn Chen, Janet Kuo, Benjamin Elder, Antonio Ojea, Lior Lieberman, Michelle Au, and Braydon Kains across Kubernetes SIGs, etcd, containerd, Gateway API, CEL admission policies, and agent sandboxes.
  • SFSCON (South Tyrol Free Software Conference) 2026 (November 13–14, 2026) — Bolzano, Italy. One of Europe's longest-running Free Software conferences bringing together public-sector decision-makers and developers to advance digital sovereignty and open infrastructure.

🗓️ December 2026

  • Yocto Project Virtual Summit 2026.12 (December 1–3, 2026) — Virtual. Community summit for embedded Linux engineers and maintainers building custom, reproducible Linux distributions across edge and IoT hardware.
  • Open Source Summit Japan 2026 (December 7–9, 2026) — Tokyo, Japan. The Linux Foundation's premier Asia-Pacific conference connecting open source developers, kernel maintainers, and enterprise leaders across cloud, embedded Linux, and open AI, including sessions from Google engineers such as Anurag Sinha.
  • OpenCompliance Summit 2026 (December 10–11, 2026) — Tokyo, Japan. Specialized gathering uniting legal, security, and OSPO practitioners around OpenChain, SPDX, software bills of materials (SBOMs), and global open source supply-chain compliance.

Open Source Reads and Links

  • [Blog] Meet the A2A CLI: discover, message, and manage agents from your terminal — In Developer Relations, few things beat showing a protocol live in a terminal during a conference talk without a complex web stack in the way. The new Apache 2.0 A2A CLI lets you discover, message, and wrap any stdin/stdout script into a streaming Agent2Agent server with --exec—raising an interesting question: does meeting developers in the Unix shell matter more for open protocol adoption than heavy SDKs?
  • [Blog] Talking to Agents with a2a (as a human!) — Right after the MCP Dev Summit in Toronto, Marc Dougherty shared a post that uncovered even more about the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol by flipping the lens from autonomous systems to human-to-agent interfaces with A2UI. Building a2term so agents render interactive terminal confirmation forms before acting raises a compelling question: could open agent protocols also save humans from enterprise UI bloat?
  • [Article] Dreamforce 2026 — When major enterprise platforms start telling customers they may never need to log into a web UI again because every workflow is now an API, MCP tool, or CLI command, where does the user interface go? RedMonk's Rachel Stephens examines this shift toward headless software and asks a question every open source protocol builder should ponder: when third-party agents mediate our data and workflows, how well does trust actually travel?
  • [Blog] EmbeddingGemma 2: an open, lightweight multimodal embedding model — Moving RAG setups fully on-device opens up real-world possibilities—from kiosks in low-connectivity areas and offline backup systems to hardware that ships with all of its own help and support docs onboard. With Google DeepMind's Apache 2.0 release of EmbeddingGemma 2 fitting multimodal search into 567MB of RAM, what new resilient tools become possible when devices don't need an internet connection to know how they work?
  • [Blog] Atproto Web Tile Embeds — Seeing AT Protocol Web Tiles in the wild sparks curiosity about what new publishing patterns become possible when open protocols move beyond text and static images. Nathan Cassell walks through embedding a live, sandboxed 3D Web Tile straight from a personal data server into a blog post—making us wonder what developers might build when interactive micro-apps can travel anywhere without phoning home.
  • [Report] Navigating Open Source Governance in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: The 2026 State of OSPOs and Open Source Management — Working in an OSPO myself, seeing how other teams operate is essential for improving how we serve as liaisons between our organizations and the broader open source ecosystem. With the Linux Foundation and TODO Group's 2026 survey finding 79% of AI-involved OSPOs shaping model policy and 69% piloting agentic workflows, how can we ensure enterprise AI governance also supports upstream maintainers?
  • [Report] Celebrating 35 Years of Linux: The Open Source Engine Powering Three Decades of Global Innovation and Infrastructure — It is incredible to see the success of the Linux kernel and distributions across enterprise software development—and to ponder how a project from the early 1990s has kept up with so many technological shifts. As Linux Foundation Research celebrates 35 years of Linux across billions of devices and every top-500 supercomputer, how can the community's model of continuous adaptation guide the next generation of maintainers?

Which of these stories will you be chatting about at your next meetup or conference? Let us know! Share with us on our @GoogleOSS X account or our @opensource.google Bluesky account.
